title: Cottonwood Travel Guide

hero.headline: Cottonwood Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Use Cottonwood as a relaxed Verde Valley base for Old Town, the Verde River, Arizona wine country, and nearby red-rock adventures.

overview: Cottonwood sits in the Verde Valley between high desert and river corridor, making it an easy base for combining food, wine, paddling, state-park trails, and nearby historic towns.
Old Town is compact enough to explore on foot, while the Verde River and Dead Horse Ranch State Park put outdoor recreation only minutes from the commercial core.

highlights.title: Old Town Cottonwood
highlights.description: Walkable tasting rooms, restaurants, shops, and historic storefronts make Old Town the city's natural first stop.

highlights.title: Verde River
highlights.description: The river adds a green riparian corridor to an otherwise dry landscape and supports paddling, wildlife viewing, and riverside recreation.

highlights.title: Arizona wine country
highlights.description: Cottonwood is a hub of the Verde Valley wine scene, with tasting rooms in town and vineyards spread through the surrounding valley.

highlights.title: Dead Horse Ranch State Park
highlights.description: This Arizona state park beside Cottonwood offers lagoons, trails, camping, and Verde River access; it is not a municipal city park.

thingsToDo.title: Walk Old Town Cottonwood
thingsToDo.description: Start in Old Town for tasting rooms, independent shops, restaurants, and the city's most visitor-friendly pedestrian blocks.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Dead Horse Ranch State Park
thingsToDo.description: Use the park for easy trails, lagoons, birding, and Verde River access. Check Arizona State Parks conditions and fees before arriving.

thingsToDo.title: Paddle or walk along the Verde River
thingsToDo.description: Guided paddling and riverside trails reveal Cottonwood's riparian ecology and are especially pleasant outside the hottest part of summer.

thingsToDo.title: Taste the Verde Valley wine scene
thingsToDo.description: Cottonwood's tasting rooms make it possible to sample regional wines without driving between vineyards; arrange transportation if drinking.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Tuzigoot National Monument
thingsToDo.description: A short drive from Cottonwood, this National Park Service site preserves a hilltop pueblo and offers context on the Verde Valley's Indigenous history.

thingsToDo.title: Pair Cottonwood with Jerome or Sedona
thingsToDo.description: Jerome and Sedona are separate destinations, but both work well as regional day trips when you keep enough time for Cottonwood itself.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Spring and fall are the easiest seasons for outdoor time
bullets: Spring and fall usually bring comfortable temperatures for walking, paddling, and trail use.
Summer afternoons can be very hot; put river and trail activities early in the day.
Winter is quieter and can be cool, especially mornings and evenings.

travelTips: Old Town is compact, but a car is useful for state parks, vineyards, Tuzigoot, Jerome, and Sedona.
Reserve popular wine, paddling, and guided outdoor experiences on weekends.
Carry water and sun protection even when the Verde River makes the landscape look lush.

faq.q: How many days do I need in Cottonwood?
faq.a: Two days works well for Old Town, the river, and one regional excursion; three gives more room for wine or hiking.

faq.q: Is Cottonwood the same destination as Sedona?
faq.a: No. Cottonwood is a separate Verde Valley city west of Sedona with its own river, wine, and Old Town identity.

faq.q: Is Dead Horse Ranch a city park?
faq.a: No. Dead Horse Ranch is an Arizona state park next to Cottonwood.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Cottonwood is an incorporated Verde Valley city whose visitor appeal comes from the combination of Old Town, the Verde River, nearby public lands, and Arizona wine country.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The Verde River corridor provides riparian habitat through a broader high-desert setting, while surrounding mesas and mountains connect Cottonwood to Sedona, Jerome, and the larger Verde Valley.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Old Town preserves the city's commercial heritage, while nearby Tuzigoot and other sites place modern Cottonwood within a much longer Indigenous history.

sections.heading: Outdoor highlights
paragraphs: River paddling, state-park trails, birding, cycling, and regional hiking complement the food and wine scene.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Walk Old Town, but use a car or guided transportation for the wider valley and neighboring destinations.
